skills.name: repurpose-content
skills.description: Turn one approved source, such as a research report, webinar, workshop, annual report, or article, into channel-native assets (newsletter section, social posts per platform, blog post, talking points, slide, email, partner kit) without drifting from what the source says. Builds a source claim register so every claim traces to the source, keeps each statistic with its source, base, and date, sets reading level per audience, adds alt text and captions, and classifies every adaptation as Format only, Wording change, or New claim or audience so staff know how much review it needs. Use when asked to repurpose, adapt, cut down, reuse, or turn an approved report or webinar into posts, emails, talking points, or a partner toolkit. Do not use for writing new content from scratch, a single LinkedIn post from an idea (linkedin-post-from-idea), or drafting a whole newsletter issue (newsletter-issue-draft).

skills.name: research-competitive-positioning
skills.description: Research a business's competitive landscape, including direct competitors, substitutes, adjacent options, and the status quo; compare target audiences, positioning, claims, proof, pricing and offers, conversion paths, content and acquisition channels; identify category patterns, risks, and credible whitespace; and produce an evidence-labeled handoff for marketing, ICP, product, sales, or brand strategy. Use when given free text, a URL, company or product materials, a competitor list, or another skill or agent's output and is asked for competitor discovery, competitive analysis, positioning maps, channel intelligence, messaging comparisons, differentiation opportunities, market-entry research, or current competitor research.

skills.name: research-grant-prospects
skills.description: Research and qualify grant funders for a nonprofit or mission-driven program - define the funding need, gather evidence from funder guidelines, IRS Form 990-PF grant lists, annual reports, peer organizations' funders and CRM history, score each prospect with a tunable weighted rubric (mission, population, geography, grant size, funding type, open or invitation only, recent giving, relationship path), and build a prospect pipeline with stages and next actions. Every funder fact is cited with source and date, and stale data is flagged. Use when asked to find foundations or corporate funders, build or clean a grant prospect list, read a 990-PF, rank funders by fit, decide which funders to approach this quarter, or plan cultivation before a letter of inquiry. Do not use for writing the proposal (write-grant-proposal), drafting a letter of inquiry (grant-letter-of-inquiry prompt), or individual donor segmentation and major-gift research.

skills.name: review-sales-forecast
skills.description: Run a weekly or quarterly sales forecast review that ends in a defensible number. Applies forecast categories (commit, best case, pipeline, omitted) with explicit inclusion criteria, inspects deals against evidence using MEDDPICC correctly, triangulates stage-weighted, historical-conversion and rep-judgement forecasts, checks pipeline coverage by stage against the team's own win rates, analyses slippage, pushes and aging, and writes the forecast narrative with risks and upside. Use when asked to prepare or run a forecast call, pressure-test a commit, call the quarter, review pipeline coverage, inspect deals for a forecast, or explain why the forecast moved. Do not use for building a mutual action plan with a buyer (use mutual-action-plan), for reviewing customer churn risk (use churn-risk-review), or for setting annual quotas (use plan-sales-territories).

skills.name: route-analytics-domains
skills.description: Recommend an approved analytics data domain for a question using a versioned domain catalog. Use before query planning when several authorized domains could fit; do not use to reveal schemas, write SQL, or grant data access.

skills.name: run-month-end-close
skills.description: Run, document, and speed up a month-end close for a small-to-mid-size company: a business-day close calendar (BD-3 to BD+10) with owners, pre-close and cutoff procedures, the core checklist (cash and bank reconciliations, AR and AP subledger ties, revenue recognition review, accruals, prepaids, fixed assets, payroll, intercompany, deferred revenue roll-forward, inventory), journal entry review standards, balance-sheet reconciliations, flux analysis against user-set thresholds, sign-off and lock, and a faster-close plan. Use when asked to build a close checklist or calendar, reconcile accounts, review journal entries, run a flux review, or shorten the close. Do not use to explain one budget variance (budget-variance-explainer), for a 13-week cash forecast (build-cash-forecast), or for accounting-standard opinions.

skills.name: steel-design
skills.description: Build enterprise SaaS application surfaces — data tables, list views, dashboards, settings, admin panels, detail/inspector panels, multi-step flows, command palettes — that read as designed rather than assembled. Use when building or redesigning any in-app product surface, CRUD screen, internal tool or admin UI; when a table needs columns, sorting, filters, bulk actions, pagination or empty states; when a form needs validation timing, progressive disclosure or a destructive-action pattern; when an app screen feels cluttered, cramped, "too much chrome", inconsistent, or like a marketing page wearing an app costume. A capability catalog of grounded UX/UI decision rules with real numbers — chrome budget, app type scale, 4px spacing, control tiers and hit targets, table anatomy, product-UI motion, WCAG 2.2 AA — plus drop-in React + Tailwind v4 reference implementations. Do not use for marketing pages, landing pages, or visual-style exploration.

skills.name: verify-design-claims
skills.description: Verify concrete claims in architecture documents, implementation plans, refactoring proposals, or state-machine designs against source evidence and executable models. Use when correctness depends on named APIs, paths, invariants, transitions, ordering, retries, or behavioral preservation.

skills.name: verify-source-claims
skills.description: Screen factual claims against supplied, versioned source passages and produce a citation-preserving review register. Use for research, reports, and agent output verification; do not treat a model score as proof or search for missing evidence without authorization.

skills.name: write-funder-report
skills.description: Write interim and final grant reports to a funder - extract every deliverable and reporting requirement from the grant agreement, build an outcomes vs targets table with honest variance explanations, write the budget-to-actual narrative explaining every variance beyond the funder's threshold, record lessons learned and course corrections, include participant stories only with recorded consent, complete an attachments checklist, set the next-period plan, and plan a stewardship follow-up. Tone is candid about shortfalls. Use when asked to write a grant report, progress or interim report, final or close-out report, answer a funder's reporting template, explain underspending or missed targets to a funder, or prepare a renewal-ready report. Do not use for a general budget variance memo (budget-variance-explainer prompt), a short update email to a funder (funder-update-email prompt), the original proposal (write-grant-proposal), or drafting the participant story itself (write-impact-story).

skills.name: write-grant-proposal
skills.description: Develop a complete grant proposal from a funder's RFP or guidelines - parse every requirement into a compliance matrix (sections, questions, word and character limits, attachments, format rules, eligibility, deadline, and where each is answered), write the need statement from cited evidence, program design, SMART objectives, organizational capacity and sustainability, hand off the logic model, evaluation plan and budget narrative, reuse approved boilerplate with freshness checks, and run a reviewer read-through against the funder's scoring criteria and a final submission checklist. Use when asked to write a grant application, answer a funder's proposal questions, turn an RFP into an outline, check a draft against guidelines, or fit a proposal to limits. Do not use for a letter of inquiry (grant-letter-of-inquiry prompt), commercial RFP responses (rfp-response-drafter prompt), the budget itself (build-grant-budget), or post-award reports (write-funder-report).

skills.name: write-impact-story
skills.description: Build ethical impact stories for a nonprofit from program notes, interviews, or participant submissions. Starts with a story bank that records consent status for every person (Consent on file, Needs consent, Do not use), applies de-identification and labelled composite rules, adds extra protections for minors (parent or guardian consent plus the organization's review), and writes strengths-based stories in the participant's own voice with quote approval, no clinical claims, and no before-and-after rescue narrative. Produces formats for short social posts, newsletter features, grant or funder report vignettes, and speech excerpts. Use when asked to write a participant story, impact story, beneficiary spotlight, donor appeal story, or vignette for a funder report from program notes or interviews. Do not use for commercial customer case studies (customer-case-study prompt), program statistics without a person's story, or general fundraising copy.

skills.name: write-in-my-voice
skills.description: Build a consented writing-style profile from a person's own writing, then draft, revise, audit, and refine text against that profile. Use when the subject directly authorizes style analysis or asks to make a draft sound more like their writing. This skill does not clone speech or audio, impersonate another person, or send or publish content.

skills.name: write-safe-mental-health-content
skills.description: Write or review mental-health content (social posts, articles, emails, event pages, press materials, video scripts) using recognized safe-messaging practice and non-stigmatizing, people-first language. Produces a review with every finding labelled Must fix, Should fix, or Consider and a specific rewrite for each, places crisis resources using the organization-approved slot, adds content notes where needed, checks images and headlines, writes a comment moderation plan for social posts, and says when to route to the organization's clinical or safety reviewer. Use when drafting or checking anything that mentions suicide, self-harm, a death, a mental-health crisis, or mental illness, including memorial and awareness-month campaigns. Do not use for a quick one-pass check (safe-messaging-review prompt), clinical advice or risk assessment, or general copyediting.
